facts.text: High Point’s Centennial Station Arts Center, housed in a historic freight train depot, serves as the town’s cultural hub.
The town’s name reflects its slightly higher elevation, standing noticeably above the surrounding lowlands in a largely flat coastal region.
A large portion of High Point once belonged to industrialist Charles Deering’s estate, whose legacy shaped early development and preservation.
High Point’s COHAB SPACE, originally a bridge between the local community and the global design industry, now hosts art and design firms amid shops and restaurants.
The Songwriters Circle, a constructive workshop for musicians of all types, is featured on the High Point Arts Council’s calendar of events.
Lynn University, a distinguished private institution, anchors High Point’s economy and contributes to the area’s intellectual and cultural vibrancy.
